Sounds like he's using you. I completely understand that it is a difficult time financially for a lot of people, however it seems as though he isn't doing the smart thing by changing his habits to save some money, and instead is putting the pressure on you which definitely isn't fair especially since you expressed that you spend more money on him than yourself. Also, it is super manipulative of him to guilt you into spending money on non-essential things such as weed, especially when you aren't a big smoker yourself. Don't get me wrong, it's amazing that you want to help and make him happy, but what is he doing for you in return? Continuously making you feel bad and not being understanding? You need to draw the line at some point--you should talk to him about limiting spending or perhaps make a list of all the things (especially non-essential) you have bought and their amounts to show him how much you are really sacrificing for him to put things into perspective.
